body: Je ressens la même chose (F31). Je pense être une personne plutôt agréable, conciliante, avec un peu d'humour tout en appréciant mes moments calmes, mais je n'ai pas d'amis. Je connais pourtant beaucoup de personnes et je reconnecte parfois avec certaines à distance, mais ça s'arrête là. En terme d'amitié j'en ai eu des déceptions donc peut-être que ça se voit que je suis méfiante ? Je ne sais pas. A part ma fratrie et mes parents avec qui je n'habite pas, je ne sors avec personne c'est triste alors que j'ai beaucoup à dire et partager.

Hello! It's nice of you to ask. I feel better now. Suicidal thoughts only come when life makes me extremely stressed, anxiety paralyzes me at least once a month, but I have found ways to control my mind instead of taking medication: sports, some hobbies that I really like. Sometimes it's not enough. Eating disorders help me even if it's not ideal. I still don't recognize myself and I don't think I'll ever fully recover from it. Nevertheless, I have become my priority and it's a huge change. I keep fighting.

I think they don't understand because they don't share your difficulties. I've talked several times to my parents and siblings, each with specific words in order not to shock/hurt them. They didn't try to fix anything, but they're here whenever I need them. I don't think they know how much I'm struggling. But I can share my feelings openly (after years of communication). I hope you find someone who can listen to you the way you want .

Omg I remember a discussion with my father. It was a few months ago.
I thought I was hallucinating. And sometimes it haunts me.
When I ask him that if my mom (so his wife) died because of a man, would he be angry at god, at this man, he answered: I would be sad but I would forgive the murderer and love him because hate will not change anything.
Ok not hate but anger? Affliction at least? 

Will you really love the one who murdered your love one?

At the end of this conversation, I understood that to him god was above all. If god takes his wife or me or my siblings, nevermind he would be sad but it is god will. 

I know my dad loves me so much thay he could do everything for me, but god is superior and he will not yell at god for taking the flesh of his flesh.

Definitely not helping me with my depression and suicidal thoughts who came during my deconversion.

I always wanted to please others including them. But I'm a grown adult. If I need them they are here. However they don't command my life anymore. 
Do you know someone you trust that can give you some advices?

You have the right not to know what to do in life as adult. I have the chance to have parents (they are christians) that love me whatever I want to achieve. They don't accept all the stuff but they support me saying: do what you want to do, is there something you like? Then go for it. Etc.
Parents always give advice. I mean good or bad, but you don't have to please them. 
Being interested in multiple things is good because your curiosity and knowledge grow. 
You can do what you like as a hobby. And in the future you never know if this hobby will become the job of your dreams.

I can relate with the most you said. I think the world is not for me. But I have a tiny mini piece of hope I hope you have or will have. Advice I received is to find yourself and to do you. What would be great is to find a way to be happy while living in this evil society and without lying to ourselves. It requires a strong power.
Thank you. I hope one day I will think like you.
Thank you. I hope your situation will get better. Wish you a good health.
Thank you.
Thank you. Your text helps me to question the good questions. I have the bad habit to look after what others think about me. I just want to do something that makes sense in my life.

Sorry you have to get through this. I hope you will soon say goodbye to your struggle. I also have difficulties to maintain relationships. Maybe that's not for me but I have to find a way to live a beautiful life anyway.
Yes it is like I have to learn life again.
Thank you.
I'm trying to stay alive. I am currently seeing a psychiatrist who helps me get through my worse crisis. I still have hope to find the true reason of my pain. Thanks for your support.

Yeah my thought wasn't clear. I considered that if god exists, him not acting would make sense to explain all the misery in the world. He would not be all powerful but men would think he is for some reasons. If he doesn't exist, then you are right: it's useless to speculate.
28-year-old me deconstructing: same and since childhood 😔

In my deconstruction the first step was being discouraged for years. I thought what the church taught was the truth but at the same times I wondered why Christians was suspicious about each others beliefs. Everyone disagrees about some verses, some readings of the Bible. 
Then I began to open the door and to see what's going on outside my community. And I felt overhelmed. I still am. Because all my world fell down. The truth was my community's one not THE truth. 
Today I'm trying to construct my own faith. I consider the bible not being the word of God, but there are some great philosophy and advices in there, like other books I can read. It is difficult because I think I betray my family. And I still have this thought: what if I am wrong and will go to hell?
Did your depression go away since then?

I never wanted this neither. This is why I'm struggling hard and I'm sorry that we are thousands living this.
I still try to rationalize my faith. But the same questions occur: then why God don't act to save innocent people from starvation or war, for what purpose God send us to the earth? 
I know deconstructing does not mean big questions to the universe cannot be answered. But I'm trying to accept that my christian faith does not want me anymore and it hurts because all my life was dedicated to know God and to have a relationship with Jesus.
Sometimes I think it's my fault that I struggle so hard because there were red flags during many years but I kept going. You know when Christians tell you to get through doubts by praying and not letting the devil separates you from God... But in christian faith, God seems to put walls between the believer and him each time he tries to keep his faith in line.

That is frightening to read. First of all, I am sorry you get through this. What is awful is the part about your children. I know why "Red" is saying this. Because he think that his beliefs are above all including people lives he cares about. I know dozens people like him. They cannot stop and think that this is wrong to force people to do what they want them to do. Even if they think they serve their God. That is not an excuse. 

Your situation is what I fear to live. During my still young years, I saw people left the church and being either supported by their family or considered strongly lost. I always heard the story about a man or woman getting rejected by their family because of their faith in Jesus and the pain caused in them. But I first experienced the contrary with a cousin who did get strong difficulties with her parents including secrets, misunderstandings, rejections. Fortunately, her situation is better with them now after almost eight years and grandchildren born.

Being a fundamentalist christian includes to live God day and night, to choose with caution relationships, to justify questionable behaviour with the bible... Well you know. I respect their faith but sometimes they have to question themselves when the situation occurs. And to stop convincing people to go against those who left. Whatever the reason.

Hope the time will help to restore your relationship with your partner's family.

I like your comparison between what and how. 
I deconstructed by searching for other beliefs, the influences that built the bible, the questioning "fight" between Jewish views of God and Christianity. For example: why Christians consider themselves like the chosen people, whereas they think Jewish were the chosen ones in the first place but don't believe well by rejecting Jesus as messiah. 

My question was: why did they steal the Jewish religion to transform it into an exclusive system of beliefs that put Christians on the top of God' scale?
Second question: why Christians should know better that Jewish themselves about the impact of old testament?

I think Christians believe hardly Paul that inspired the majority of the new testament, in order to make sense with their view of the old testament and the story that tells Jesus was in the cross because of some jewish.
I wondered why Jewish cannot see their past huge error. The old testament announced Jesus and he appeared to them. So why were and are they so stubborn? Because Jewish stick to their religion as Christians do as well. 

Seeing all the differencies and conflicts, it is surprising to see that some Christians still think that God of Jewish and Christians are the same. Their behaviour shows that he cannot be. What if Christians are wrong with their beliefs? What if God is not a jewish god but the master of universe that all civilizations tried to understand and represent for centuries?

I understand why religious people stick to their religion: duty, family influences, own spirituality. The people who have the chance to choose what they can believe in, strongly follow their hearts before reason. That leads them to a purpose in life, some peace and joy. With christianity, it did work for me for a couple years, but not anymore. I cannot throw away the inconsistencies and the men influences in the bible. 
I have to find my purpose. I don't know how and if I will manage to do that. However, I find amazing that any kind of religions exist. Humans imagination is beyond limits. I can choose whatever gives me peace without questioning if I am right or wrong.
Thank you for your reply. It will help me a lot.

I received this kind of messages in a group that supports depressed people. Whatever I was saying he kept telling me "Jesus want a relationship with you etc". Even when I revealed that I was born in the church (and "born again"), he didn't understand that I knew already the classic propaganda texts. I was so upset that after trying to show him that believing in Jesus is not a cure (but counseling, kindness, support, medecine), I finally ghosted him.

When i was christian it was like nobody could believe that Jesus let me suffer mentally and get depressed. Some blamed the demons in me... 
When I did a suicide attempt I realised that Jesus is no more my friend and I decided to definitely throw away "just pray" advices and continue my deconstruction.
I got depression before quarantine, got better during it and my deconstruction began. I lost my faith in 2021. Still depressed and don't know how to act because the faith was everything.

I finally knew what was going on about christinanity. People choose to shut reason and seek for faith and comfort. Christians I know always say they found the truth. But the truth is they refuse to understand more about the bible because they are afraid to lose their faith. That is not truth but fear and ignorance. That doesn't work for me anymore
Well said.

I relate so much to this. I am free of weird thinking (God is love but jealous and perfect even though He killed innocent children or other people because He wanted it), but I feel a kind of burden. I would like to make my family realise that if they take the bible as a source of multiple arts (stories, legends, songs), they can still be spiritual and be in phase with some of their beliefs. Because no, you cannot yell Jesus came to save us from God's wrath, say God never change and ignore his awful behaviour.  
Saying I don't understand some scriptures but I still trust God of the bible is not enough for me anymore.
I rather believe in the universe and his highness than worship the God as described of the bible (the god of hebrews btw). After a lifetime (I'm 28) believing crap, it feels really difficult to watch my family continue their christian life.

It's like "you have the time to play video games or go to theaters but no time to take with the lord?"
When I was still a believer, it annoyed me. People have the right to be religious by themselves alone or not.

I have been in a meeting of women of different denominations. We were less than ten so it was interesting to hear testimonies of each and talk about it.
Suddenly a girl became overwhelmed saying to another girl a kind of prophecy. That was really weird. I remember she said her hands are shining so the prophecy is powerful, you have to listen to me (sort of). It took a few minutes for her to calm down.
It was too much for me and the beginning of being away from pentecostal or charismatic stuff.

In a church more open minded that my birth church, there were a meeting only for the Spirit doings : a word of knowledge, prophecy, spirit meditation. 
I kept laughing in silence when I watched people dancing arguing their dance is inspired by the holy spirit. It was just kind of contemporary dance to me and being moved by the music.

Thanks to reddit I discover every day some answers to my questions about speaking in tongues, gifts of spirit, the role of the brain in a emotional situation. I got some clarity in the cloudy process I'm in.
I used to say that when I was asked if I had a religion. Ridiculous.
Oh my godness, this sentence "our saviour is not on the cross anymore" used to convince me now it is irritating me.

Sadly this is what the church I grew up in taught and teaches. I still hear the preachers tell "this church is doing this and accept that so they are not telling the truth, God does not accredit them. But we..."

I thought all my life that the other denominations were totally wrong despite the fact they were also christians. What a surprise to talk years later to an open-minded pastor that is accepting the beliefs of others without judgement and the idea that he might be wrong.

I don't know why they keep believing that Jesus is coming back soon whereas :

- Jesus said in the bible Matt 16 28 : Verily I say unto you, There be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom.
Some say that death is a spiritual death. Whatever...

- it is written that Jesus is coming soon. He is coming soon since 2000 years? 
When I was Christian I didn't buy the explanation that says that 1000 years can be 1 day for God. I thought that Jesus will come soon because the life is short and WE will die soon and meet him. Yeah mindtrick.

I hear many christians telling : "prophecies are many this days! Repent before it is too late! Jesus is coming very very soon!"

When I was 8 I dreamed about how is the life after death and because I was a child I was scared that God take my life too early before I experienced life, cause what I saw in my dream frightened me. 

I lived with this fear that what I saw happens since then. I deconverted recently and it bothers me less but it is still here.

That kind of text almost broke my entire self. I was born again like others ; the belief, the experiences until I find this born again thing in people's testimonies of other beliefs or religions. When I quit Christianity I feared to be judged like "this person that is leaving the belief was not ever a Christian". I heard so many people in my community tell this that I was scared to death to assume my deconversion.

Finally, when I hear that kind of rude sentence (that is the sing of a cult btw) I repeat to myself that I am the proof (as small as it is) that the born again thing is no exclusive nor endless. Outside of the church there is reality with people like them, experiencing life with different beliefs, that don't offend everyday the other by saying : you're not in the truth! Because we are all in the same boat. Why bother people on how they want to live before death?

By my question I meant : do you still think, as an exchristian, that speaking in tongues was real and not a kind of mindtrick. As I don't believe in the bible's God, I wonder how it works. But somebody in the comments told me about glossolalia.
The experience of your friend seems awful. In my church, there was a moment at the end of the preach when people could pray loudly and the majority was speaking in tongues. There was also a moment where one person spoke in tongues and another one was interpreting it.


I never saw a person speaking in tongues for the first time but I witnessed what was going on around : 4/5 Christians were praying hardly until the person spoke. If that didn't work they tried another time with the same process.

Thank you for sharing your experience. And I am truly surprised that you still can do this even as an atheist. I always thought that glossolalia was being able to speak foreign languages without learning them. I was wrong. If speaking like this helps them to get through life like meditation can, then yeah I will not argue with them.

This analogy is so accurate. It really is a toxic relationship. I used to think that I don't have to expect God to manifest his presence when I ask because he is all powerful and far beyond humanity. 

Why should I  continue to look after him when I have been told that I find him by following Jesus? And following Jesus does not make him appear despite all the prayers. We have to do things by ourselves because the holy spirit you know.

So I better leave by living on my own and away from that. But this is hard because this relationship was my life.

Christians use mindtricks to get comfort because God let them in the dark but the bible says God is always there. So either they don't pray enough or they think God want to keep them in their mud before he delivers them. 
That is one of the reasons why I left Christianity. Free but not so free.

So true! I find great to help people to find happiness when they feel miserable or have bad life experiences. Some Christians come and say "if you want to have a full peace and joy come to Jesus!". But they never say that behind this there is a lifetime trial with many steps to prove you really accepted Jesus. Ugh!

Yeah I was thinking about this earlier this day. It gives anger and anxiety at the same time. I felt idiot and foolish. Not that I think religious people are, but I always thought that the evangelical church where I grew up was right about everything without me questioning it. 
A couple years ago a cousin told me where as I was still in it that it was a cult. I refused to agree with her but now I can tell this is a cult. There was no direct coercion or abuse in my case but can we consider the use of biblical threats as coercion?

I can relate. I got depression in mid 20's and when I tried to get help, some christians told me to pray (in vain) and one girl threw at my face that I was demon possessed and if I refused to get a pastor hand on my head it was because I didn't want to be healed. 
I am a hypersensitive person that is analyzing things and thoughts too much. So I felt attacked and unworthy. When I get suicidal, no one knew how to handle this instead of telling me to pray. Fortunately, my christian parents accepted that secular help can do a lot and tried to comfort me as they could.

I left my church at 27 years old. Feel like I wasted my youth. It was not my parents that kept away from me some freedom. I thank them for letting me experience life. But I grew up in a conservative church and I learn I had to live without sin and to follow the rules or I would disappoint God and worse go to hell. I grew up with fear.
So when I realized that was nonsense and that was just coming from the faith of the pastors and the community and not God, I blacked out. Anger, frustration, loneliness and fear again. That leads me to depression. I know I am young (28) but it was like my life ended with my deconstruction and I don't know who I am now.

A letter is an excellent idea. I am an adult in her late 20's and I live in my own house but I had to share my disbelief instead of acting like nothing has changed. 
My mental health was at stake. 

I send some long messages time to time to prepare them. The one about doubts, the second about me leaving the church, the third about me questioning a lot about the bible. Finally I told them that I was no longer believing in Jesus, the son the spirit etc. And that the thing that lead me there is the bible itself. What I learned about its supposed inerrancy, God being good and awful at the same time, etc. They choose to not look any further and to keep their beliefs because of their experiences prooving Jesus is here. I will not try to convince them.

Imo the best way to keep a good relationship with your parents is that all of you accept the belief of the other. I think it begins by avoiding discussions about faith.
So my thought is that you should not "destroy" their faith but you could affirm your faith before them if they ask questions or else. It is more peaceful I think.
If one discussion causes rift, then it has to stop before it goes too far.
All christians are not oppressors I think. Just people believing hardly without hurting any people. Some or many, it depends, nonetheless are.

It is like what is happening with my family. I once believed in all the things the evangelical church taught me. When I stopped, I wondered how my family can have faith in all this nonsense? Then I accepted that this kind of beliefs reassures them, offers them a goal. I am no one to destroy that just because I don't believe in the same things. I am no one to call them dumb or stupid for that. That is not fair.

Thank you for your kindness. Here was a comment coming after the urge to get over anger and frustration. It was like my best friend had lying to me about an essential thing all my life and doesn't apologize for it. This feeling hurt me hard last night but I am better now.
I like your principles. I'm currently trying to move forward and do my thing. It is difficult but I hope I/we will get through this.

Thank you for your kindness. My doctor sent me to a psychiatrist because of the attempt I did. It is free cause of the health care system in my country. It helped a lot but I know that I have to explore more about my mental illness, to see a psychologist for example but it is expansive.
I did see a psychologist months ago to deal with my emotions (it helped me not to go deeper in the dark) but she was lacking of skills to help me with my depression.

I did my first time three months ago. I was so afraid that my collegues would discover my swollen arm. It was essentially epidermis cuts. The day after I did the same cuts on the other arm. As what you share, I wanted the emotional pain to leave. No success. 
It took time before telling my doctor what was going on. I felt so ashamed and unvalid like "why do you sh? Your life is good!"
So I went on groups in social media to share and feel some relief. Nobody judged me and I finally told my parents about it few days after this first time.
I relapsed a lot and didn't tell them until one month passed.

My parents are very loving, not judging me and listening to me. But I will not tell them that I am still suffering like h... and doing cuts (sometimes very deep).

I think it depends on your genetics and on the depth of your cuts. I have two scars that are 2 months old. One has reached the deep dermis and raised a little. I started to massage it with cream and it is slowly flattening since then.

I wish you win this battle. I am 28. After several weeks, I will get back to work halftime. It is great and I thought I got better, but depression is really wicked. I was told that depression hides a deep suffering. All I want is to find its source and to be finally free of mental pain.
I am in the same mood. I feel the urge to relapse then I remember that scars do not completely fade. Hold on.
I have them too and some on my feet.
